questions.questionText: She _____ to the gym every morning.
questions.explanation: Present simple with third-person singular 'she' requires 'goes'.

questions.questionText: Look! It _____ outside.
questions.explanation: Present continuous is used for actions happening right now.

questions.questionText: I _____ this book since last week.
questions.explanation: 'Since' indicates present perfect continuous for an action that started in the past and continues.

questions.questionText: They _____ here for five years.
questions.explanation: 'For' indicates a duration; present perfect is used for an action that started in the past and continues.

questions.questionText: He _____ his keys yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' indicates past simple tense.

questions.questionText: We _____ dinner when the phone rang.
questions.explanation: Past continuous is used for an action in progress interrupted by another action.

questions.questionText: By the time I arrived, they _____ already left.
questions.explanation: Past perfect is used for an action completed before another past action.

questions.questionText: She _____ for three hours before she found the lost dog.
questions.explanation: Past perfect continuous shows an ongoing action before another past event.

questions.questionText: I _____ you tomorrow at 10 AM.
questions.explanation: Future simple is used for planned future events.

questions.questionText: This time tomorrow, I _____ on the beach.
questions.explanation: Future continuous is used for an action that will be in progress at a specific future time.

questions.questionText: By next year, she _____ her degree.
questions.explanation: Future perfect is used for an action that will be completed before a specific future time.

questions.questionText: I _____ this work for two hours by lunchtime.
questions.explanation: Future perfect continuous emphasizes the duration of an action up to a future point.

questions.questionText: He has lived here _____ 2010.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time.

questions.questionText: I have _____ finished my homework.
questions.explanation: 'Already' is used in affirmative sentences with present perfect to indicate something done before expected.

questions.questionText: Have you finished your project _____?
questions.explanation: 'Yet' is used in questions with present perfect to ask about something expected.

questions.questionText: I have _____ arrived home.
questions.explanation: 'Just' is used with present perfect to indicate something that happened very recently.

questions.questionText: She _____ French for ten years.
questions.explanation: Present perfect is used with 'for' to show an action continuing from past to present.

questions.questionText: They _____ to Paris last summer.
questions.explanation: 'Last summer' indicates a finished time in the past, requiring past simple.

questions.questionText: Right now, the children _____ in the garden.
questions.explanation: 'Right now' indicates an action happening at the moment, requiring present continuous.

questions.questionText: I _____ three cups of coffee today.
questions.explanation: 'Today' is a time period continuing to the present, requiring present perfect.

questions.questionText: When I was young, I _____ to school every day.
questions.explanation: Past simple is used for completed habitual actions in the past.

questions.questionText: She was reading a book while I _____ cooking.
questions.explanation: Past continuous is used for two simultaneous ongoing past actions.

questions.questionText: He _____ already _____ his assignment before the deadline.
questions.explanation: Past perfect is used for an action completed before another past event (the deadline).

questions.questionText: We _____ dinner at 7 PM tonight.
questions.explanation: Future continuous is used for an action that will be in progress at a specific future time.

questions.questionText: She _____ never _____ sushi before.
questions.explanation: Present perfect is used with 'never' for life experiences up to now.

questions.questionText: The train _____ when we reached the station.
questions.explanation: Past perfect is used because the train left before we arrived.

questions.questionText: By 2030, scientists _____ a cure for the disease.
questions.explanation: Future perfect is used for an action that will be completed before a specific future year.

questions.questionText: I _____ for this company since 2018.
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous with 'since' emphasizes the duration of an ongoing action.

questions.questionText: She usually _____ tea in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'Usually' indicates a habitual action, requiring present simple.

questions.questionText: I _____ the movie twice already.
questions.explanation: 'Already' and 'twice' with present perfect indicate a repeated experience up to now.
